Section: section_1 — Intuitive Hook: The Sliding Window

Lecture lines:
Think of filters as sliding magnifying glasses.
Scanning photographs extracts vital visual details.
Imagine our filter detecting cat ears.

Planned animations:
Create a 3x3 grid of moving dots; fade in central highlight.
Transition grid to a sliding square window over data.
Flash the window red to signal data capture.

Section: section_2 — Mathematical Core: Element-wise Product and Sum

Lecture lines:
Convolution combines input and kernel matrices.
Multiply overlapping elements, then sum them up.
Flipping the kernel defines the operation formally.
Slide across grid to create new map.
One input pixel results from every shift.

Planned animations:
Display two vectors side-by-side using MathTex.
Animate arrows connecting corresponding vector elements.
Show product result floating below each pair.

Section: section_3 — Prerequisite Sync: Dot Products

Lecture lines:
Dot products measure how well patterns match.
High values indicate strong pattern alignment.
Convolution acts as a powerful feature detector.

Planned animations:
Draw two vectors as arrows from origin in #FFFFFF.
Fade in the Dot Product scalar value definition.
Highlight the scalar value in #FFD700.

Section: section_4 — Real-World Application: Image Processing & CNNs

Lecture lines:
Convolutional layers stack to form deep networks.
Simple edges evolve into complex object recognition.
Drones use convolutions to identify landing pads.

Planned animations:
Overlay a 3x3 filter on a pixelated image.
Animate the filter sliding across the grid.
Flash the output feature map cells in #00FF00.

Section: section_5 — Summary & Reflection

Lecture lines:
Convolution is scanning, multiplying, and summing.
It serves as a template matching engine.
Visualize it extracting features from data.

Planned animations:
Fade in 'Convolution' title centered in #FFFFFF.
Pop up labels: 'Sliding Window', 'Dot Product'.
Pulse all labels simultaneously to signal completion.

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
